policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: Article before the name (ὁ Ἰησοῦς) has no English exponent; ASV 'Jesus manifested himself again' renders either reading identically.
ASV 'They went forth, and entered into the boat' carries no adverb of immediacy; the added εὐθύς ('immediately') would be rendered, as ASV renders that adverb elsewhere in narrative.
ASV 'when day was now breaking' is progressive, rendering the present participle γινομένης; the aorist γενομένης gives completed 'when day was now come'.
Presence or absence of the article with Ἰησοῦς has no exponent in 'Jesus stood on the beach'.
Article before Ἰησοῦς; ASV 'Jesus therefore saith unto them' is identical under either reading.
ASV 'they were not able to draw it' does not distinguish imperfect ἴσχυον from aorist ἴσχυσαν; the past-tense English fits both, and 'now' renders οὐκέτι, not the verb's aspect.
ASV 'Simon Peter therefore went up' renders the connective οὖν; the omitting reading leaves nothing for 'therefore'.

ASV 'drew the net to land' renders motion toward, εἰς τὴν γῆν with the accusative; ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς with the genitive is locative 'on the land'. The verse's only note is an alternative_rendering ('Or, aboard') on ἀνέβη and does not bear on this unit.
ASV opens 'Jesus saith unto them' with no connective, but ASV routinely leaves narrative δέ untranslated; the English neither requires nor excludes it.
ASV 'Jesus cometh' has no connective, but an untranslated οὖν is within ASV's practice; absence of an English exponent does not exclude the particle.
Article before Ἰησοῦς has no English exponent in 'Jesus cometh'. The note 'Or, loaf' is an alternative_rendering on ἄρτον and does not decide a reading.
Article with the proper name; 'that Jesus was manifested' is the same under either reading.
ASV reads 'to the disciples' with no possessive; the added αὐτοῦ would give 'to his disciples', a pronoun ASV renders where present.
ASV 'Simon, son of John' with the mapped greek_gloss note 'Greek Joanes' transliterates Ἰωάννου, not Ἰωνᾶ ('son of Jonas').
ASV 'Simon, son of John' with the note 'Greek Joanes' renders Ἰωάννου; Ἰωνᾶ would give 'son of Jonas'.
ASV 'Simon, son of John' with the note 'Greek Joanes' renders Ἰωάννου, excluding Ἰωνᾶ.

Within this verse ASV keeps the historic present distinct from the past: 'He saith unto him the third time' and 'Jesus saith unto him' for λέγει, against 'And he said unto him, Lord' here, which renders the aorist εἶπεν.
Word order only; 'thou knowest all things' is the same rendering for πάντα σύ and σὺ πάντα.
Article with Ἰησοῦς; 'Jesus saith unto him' is identical either way.
ASV renders 'my sheep' with no diminutive force; πρόβατα and the diminutive προβάτια both yield 'sheep' in ASV, which marks no diminutive here.
Word order only; 'another shall gird thee' renders either sequence of σε and ζώσει.
ASV 'Peter, turning about, seeth' has no connective, but ASV commonly leaves narrative δέ unrendered; the English does not exclude it.
ASV 'Peter therefore seeing him' renders οὖν; the omitting reading leaves 'therefore' without a base.
Word order only; 'follow thou me' renders μοι ἀκολούθει and ἀκολούθει μοι alike.
Word order only; 'This saying therefore went forth' is the same for οὗτος ὁ λόγος and ὁ λόγος οὗτος.
ASV 'yet Jesus said not unto him' renders an adversative postpositive δέ; the alternative begins the clause with copulative καί, which ASV renders 'and'.
Greek article with the participial phrase; ASV 'This is the disciple that beareth witness' supplies the English article under either reading.
Word order only; 'his witness is true' renders both sequences.
ASV 'many other things which Jesus did' fits both the plain relative ἃ and the correlative ὅσα, which ASV also renders with 'which' after 'many other things'.
ASV 'would not contain' in a contrary-to-fact supposition does not distinguish the future infinitive χωρήσειν from the aorist χωρῆσαι.
ASV ends 'the books that should be written' with no closing 'Amen'; the added Ἀμήν is unrepresented.
